content: Efavirenz is known to interact with various drugs by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Below are the detailed interactions and recommendations for each drug: 1. Efavirenz and Sorafenib: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. It is recommended to avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 2. Efavirenz and Sotalol: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider an alternative therapy. 3. Efavirenz and Sotorasib: Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of sotorasib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 4. St. John’s Wort and Efavirenz: St. John’s Wort reduces the levels or effects of efavirenz by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 5. Efavirenz and Stiripentol: Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of stiripentol via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, increase the dose of stiripentol. 6. Efavirenz and Sunitinib: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 7. Efavirenz and Suvorexant: Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of suvorexant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If a higher dose of suvorexant is required, do not exceed 20 mg/day. 8. Efavirenz and Tacrolimus: Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of tacrolimus via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 9. Efavirenz and Tovorafenib: Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of tovorafenib by reducing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of tovorafenib with strong or moderate CYP2C8 inhibitors. 17. Efavirenz and Trabectedin: Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of trabectedin via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 18. Efavirenz and Trazodone: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 19. Tucatinib also increases the levels of efavirenz. Avoid coadministration with CYP3A substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious toxicities. 21.
